.quiz-cta{padding:18px 18px}}</style><style>/* Final presentation layer for lane 2 bodies (2026-11-11). Scoped to article.l2-article.df.
   Uses only the site tokens --ink, --paper, --panel, --accent. Load after L2_CSS. */
.l2-article.df{max-width:800px;font-size:18px}
.l2-article.df h1{margin-bottom:12px}
.l2-article.df h2{font-size:26px;line-height:1.25;margin:56px 0 14px}
.l2-article.df h2::after{content:"";display:block;width:56px;height:5px;border-radius:3px;background:var(--accent);margin-top:10px}
.l2-article.df h3{font-size:20px}
.l2-article.df p{line-height:1.65;margin:10px 0 16px;max-width:68ch}
.l2-article.df strong.df-k{font-weight:700}

/* jump pills under the h1 */
.l2-article.df .df-jump{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:8px;margin:0 0 20px;font:700 14px/1.3 Arial,sans-serif}
.l2-article.df .df-jump span{opacity:.75;margin-right:2px}
.l2-article.df .df-jump a{display:inline-block;padding:7px 13px;border-radius:20px;border:1.5px solid var(--ink);color:var(--ink);text-decoration:none;background:var(--paper)}
.l2-article.df .df-jump a:first-of-type{background:var(--accent);border-color:var(--accent)}

/* answer card */
.l2-article.df .df-answer{background:var(--accent);border-radius:16px;padding:22px 26px 10px;margin:4px 0 30px}
.l2-article.df .df-answer::before{content:"Quick answer";display:inline-block;background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);font:700 12px/1 Arial,sans-serif;letter-spacing:.12em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:7px 12px;border-radius:20px;margin-bottom:12px}
.l2-article.df .df-answer p{max-width:none}
.l2-article.df .df-answer p.df-lead{font-size:20px;line-height:1.5;font-weight:400}
.l2-article.df .df-answer p.df-lead > strong:first-child{display:block;font-size:23px;line-height:1.35;font-weight:800;margin-bottom:8px}
.l2-article.df .df-answer .source,.l2-article.df .df-answer .note{opacity:.9}
.l2-article.df .df-answer a{color:var(--ink)}

/* stat cards */
.l2-article.df .df-stats{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:10px;margin:16px 0 18px}
.l2-article.df .df-stats-2{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}
.l2-article.df .df-stats-3{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)}
.l2-article.df .df-stat{background:var(--paper);border-radius:12px;padding:14px 14px 12px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:5px}
.l2-article.df .df-stat-q{font:700 11px/1 Arial,sans-serif;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;opacity:.7}
.l2-article.df .df-stat-n{font:800 32px/1 Arial,sans-serif;letter-spacing:-.02em}
.l2-article.df .df-stat-t{font:14px/1.35 Arial,sans-serif;opacity:.85}

/* bar charts built from table numbers */
.l2-article.df .df-chart{margin:20px 0 6px;padding:16px 18px 12px;background:var(--panel);border-radius:14px;font:15px/1.35 Arial,sans-serif}
.l2-article.df .df-chart-t{font-weight:700;font-size:15px;margin:0 0 8px}
.l2-article.df .df-legend{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px 16px;margin:0 0 10px;font-size:13px;font-weight:700}
.l2-article.df .df-key::before{content:"";display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:3px;margin-right:6px;vertical-align:-1px;background:var(--ink)}
.l2-article.df .df-key-c::before{background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 30%,transparent)}
.l2-article.df .df-rows{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0}
.l2-article.df .df-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,38%) 1fr;gap:12px;align-items:center;margin:0;padding:6px 0;border-bottom:1px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 10%,transparent)}
.l2-article.df .df-row:last-child{border-bottom:0}
.l2-article.df .df-lab{font-weight:700;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.l2-article.df .df-bars{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 54px;gap:3px 8px;align-items:center}
.l2-article.df .df-bar{height:14px;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 8%,transparent);border-radius:7px;overflow:hidden}
.l2-article.df .df-fill{display:block;height:100%;background:var(--ink);border-radius:7px;min-width:3px}
.l2-article.df .df-bar-c{height:8px}
.l2-article.df .df-bar-c .df-fill{background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 30%,transparent)}
.l2-article.df .df-val{font-weight:700;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;text-align:right}
.l2-article.df .df-val-c{font-weight:400;font-size:13px;opacity:.8}
.l2-article.df .df-map .df-rows{position:relative;padding-left:26px}
.l2-article.df .df-map .df-rows::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:8px;top:8px;bottom:8px;width:6px;border-radius:3px;background:var(--ink);opacity:.85}
.l2-article.df .df-map .df-row{position:relative}
.l2-article.df .df-map .df-row::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:-23px;top:50%;width:12px;height:12px;margin-top:-6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--accent);border:3px solid var(--ink);box-sizing:border-box}

/* the full table under each chart, behind a native toggle */
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox{margin:4px 0 24px}
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox > summary{cursor:pointer;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font:700 14px/1.3 Arial,sans-serif;padding:8px 14px;border-radius:20px;border:1.5px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 35%,transparent);list-style:none}
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox > summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox > summary::after{content:"+";font-size:17px;line-height:1}
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox[open] > summary::after{content:"\2212"}
.l2-article.df .df-tablebox[open] > summary{margin-bottom:6px}

/* tables: rounded box, dark header, edge shadow while more columns are hidden */
.l2-article.df .l2-tablewrap{position:relative;border-radius:12px;border:1px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 18%,transparent);
  background:linear-gradient(to right,var(--paper) 30%,transparent) left center/40px 100% no-repeat local,
             linear-gradient(to left,var(--paper) 30%,transparent) right center/40px 100% no-repeat local,
             linear-gradient(to right,color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 22%,transparent),transparent) left center/14px 100% no-repeat scroll,
             linear-gradient(to left,color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 22%,transparent),transparent) right center/14px 100% no-repeat scroll}
.l2-article.df table{font-size:15px}
.l2-article.df caption{font:700 14px/1.4 Arial,sans-serif;padding:12px 12px 8px;position:sticky;left:0}
.l2-article.df thead th{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);border-color:var(--ink)}
.l2-article.df td{background:transparent;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}

/* quiz CTA: one clear action card */
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);border:0;border-radius:16px;padding:24px 26px;margin:34px 0;box-shadow:0 8px 24px color-mix(in srgb,var(--ink) 25%,transparent)}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta p{max-width:none;color:var(--paper)}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta p:first-child{font-size:19px;line-height:1.5}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta .button{background:var(--accent);color:var(--ink);border-radius:30px;padding:16px 26px;font-size:18px;margin-top:6px}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta .button::after{content:" \2192"}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta .cta-note,.l2-article.df .quiz-cta p.note{font-size:13px;opacity:.8;background:none;padding:0;border-radius:0}
.l2-article.df .quiz-cta a:not(.button){color:var(--paper)}
.l2-article.df .df-answer .quiz-cta{margin:18px -10px 18px}

/* numbered steps */

</style><article class="l2-article guide appeals-guide df" id="nj-uninsured-underinsured-motorist-appeals-decisions">
<h1>NJ Uninsured and Underinsured Motorist Appeals: What 13 Decisions Show</h1><nav class="df-jump" aria-label="Jump to" data-df="added"><span>Jump to:</span><a href="#faq">Questions</a><a href="#sources">Sources</a></nav>
<p class="byline">By Sandra H. Brown, Injuries Cases Autos research. Updated <time datetime="2026-11-11">11 November 2026</time></p>
<section id="answer" class="df-answer">
<p class="df-lead"><strong class="df-k">New Jersey appeals courts have held insurers to the UM and UIM limit on the declarations page: Motil kept 100,000 dollars against a 15,000 step-down, and Rafanello kept a commercial truck's 750,000 floor.</strong> Claims were lost on releases, late filing and unproven permanent injury.</p>
<aside class="key-facts"><ul>
<li data-origin="original"><strong>13</strong> of the 76 NJ car-case appeals in our index turn on a UM or UIM question</li>
<li data-origin="original"><strong>3</strong> of those 13 were lost because the injury was not shown to be permanent</li>
<li><strong>100,000</strong> dollars: the declared UIM limit Motil kept against a 15,000 step-down</li>
<li><strong>750,000</strong> dollars: the coverage floor for a commercial truck, listed driver or not</li>
</ul></aside>
</section>
<section class="quiz-cta" id="quiz-top">
<p>Hit by an uninsured or underinsured driver in New Jersey? A 30-second questionnaire checks whether a lawyer's office may review your claim for free.</p>
<p><a class="button" data-quiz-link="after-answer" href="https://quiz.injuriescases.autos/s/accident-newjersey?utm_source=injuriescases.autos&amp;utm_medium=referral&amp;utm_campaign=nj_mva_seo&amp;utm_content=nj-uninsured-underinsured-motorist-appeals-decisions">Start the New Jersey accident quiz</a></p>
<p class="cta-note">Advertisement. Opens the New Jersey questionnaire. Review its policies and contact consent before submitting your details. No legal advice or guarantee of acceptance or compensation.</p>
</section>
<section id="cases">
<h2>What did New Jersey's 13 UM and UIM appeals decide?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">Six were affirmed, three reversed and three mixed; the thirteenth, Campbell, is a pretrial evidence ruling with no appeal result.</strong> Nine are published and four are unpublished 2025 decisions.</p>
<p>Five came from Middlesex County, covered on our <a href="/new-jersey/middlesex-county-car-accident-help">Middlesex County crash data page</a>. For how UM and UIM coverage works in New Jersey before a claim reaches court, start with our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-uninsured-motorist-claim-help">NJ uninsured motorist claim guide</a>.</p>
<div class="table-wrap">
<div class="l2-tablewrap" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><table class="df-stack">
<caption>The 9 published UM and UIM decisions in our appeals index, newest first</caption>
<thead>
<tr><th scope="col">Decision</th><th scope="col">County</th><th scope="col">What was at stake</th><th scope="col">Result</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/10850226/noah-tenenbaum-v-allstate-insurance-company/">Tenenbaum (2026)</a></th><td data-label="County">Middlesex</td><td data-label="What was at stake">bad-faith and Insurance Fair Conduct Act claims next to a disputed UIM claim</td><td data-label="Result">mixed: bad-faith discovery stayed until the UIM case is decided; one appeal reversed, one dismissed as no longer live</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/10604340/keith-hacker-v-carlos-jaime-valdez/">Hacker (2025)</a></th><td data-label="County">Ocean</td><td data-label="What was at stake">two-vehicle crash; defendant in bankruptcy</td><td data-label="Result">reversed: 1.6 million dollar verdict ordered cut to the 200,000 of coverage the claim was limited to</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/9988098/estate-of-william-massi-v-bette-barr/">Massi (2024)</a></th><td data-label="County">Middlesex</td><td data-label="What was at stake">cyclist fell avoiding a passing pickup, no contact</td><td data-label="Result">mixed: dismissal for the townships vacated; rest affirmed</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/9491190/britney-motil-v-wausau-underwriters-insurance-company/">Motil (2024)</a></th><td data-label="County">Gloucester</td><td data-label="What was at stake">step-down from 100,000 to 15,000 after a 15,000 settlement with the at-fault driver</td><td data-label="Result">affirmed: 100,000 UIM limit kept</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/8244203/scott-c-malzberg-v-caren-l-josey-l-7858-17-essex-county-and-statewide/">Malzberg (2022)</a></th><td data-label="County">Essex</td><td data-label="What was at stake">UM or UIM issue after a left-turning car struck a motorcycle</td><td data-label="Result">affirmed</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/4888351/jose-carbajal-vs-nancy-v-patel-l-4317-17-middlesex-county-and/">Carbajal (2021)</a></th><td data-label="County">Middlesex</td><td data-label="What was at stake">phantom vehicle shared fault; 200,000 verdict</td><td data-label="Result">mixed: UM paid its 15,000 limit, the identified driver the 185,000 balance</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/4831583/ronald-rafanello-vs-jorge-s-taylor-esquivel-l-3488-15-and-l-1721-17/">Rafanello (2020)</a></th><td data-label="County">Union</td><td data-label="What was at stake">dump truck with an unlisted driver in a multi-vehicle crash</td><td data-label="Result">reversed: 750,000 commercial floor applies</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision"><a href="https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/6487865/campbell-v-allstate-ins-co/">Campbell (2019)</a></th><td data-label="County">not stated</td><td data-label="What was at stake">UM or UIM suit against Allstate after a two-car collision, before trial</td><td data-label="Result">no appeal result: defence expert barred from citing articles unless copies were produced within 20 days</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Decision">Katchen (2019)</th><td data-label="County">Morris</td><td data-label="What was at stake">motorcyclist's UM or UIM claim against GEICO</td><td data-label="Result">reversed</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
</div>

<p>Each opinion links to its free full text. Memudu and Nesby, discussed below, come from our separate UM and UIM decision file, not the 13 coded rows. All 76 rows are in our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-car-accident-appeals-index">New Jersey car accident appeals index</a>.</p>
</section>
<section id="step-down">
<h2>Can a step-down clause cut my UIM coverage to 15,000 dollars?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">Not when the declarations page promises more.</strong> In Motil (2024), the court kept the 100,000 dollar UIM limit the insurer tried to step down to 15,000.</p>
<p>Britney Motil was driving her father's Jeep, listed on her parents' policy with a different garaging address. The insurer said she was neither a named insured nor a resident relative, so the step-down applied.</p>
<div class="table-wrap">
<div class="l2-tablewrap" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"><table class="df-stack">
<caption>Motil: declared and disputed UM and UIM limits</caption>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Figure</th><th scope="col">Amount</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Figure">At-fault driver's policy limit, paid in settlement</th><td data-label="Amount">15,000 dollars</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Figure">UM and UIM limit on the declarations page</th><td data-label="Amount">100,000 dollars per person</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Figure">Step-down limit the insurer argued for</th><td data-label="Amount">15,000 per person, 30,000 per accident</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" data-label="Figure">Result on appeal</th><td data-label="Amount">100,000 dollars; trial court affirmed</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>
</div>
<figure class="article-image coverage-graphic"><img alt="Motil comparison: the declarations page stated 100,000 dollars per person; the insurer argued for a 15,000 dollar step-down; the court upheld the declared limit on those facts" decoding="async" height="1024" loading="lazy" src="https://cdn.dorik.com/6acbe74237318c00111fbd1e/images/nj-motil-coverage-limits-Mb7_R.webp" width="1536"/><figcaption>Figures from Motil (2024), not current minimums or a promised payout.</figcaption></figure>
<p>She was a covered driver, the Jeep was a covered car, and the UM premium was the same for every vehicle. Under the reasonable expectations doctrine, the policyholder's reading won.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-1">1</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section id="commercial">
<h2>Does a step-down apply to a commercial truck that hit me?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">Not below the 750,000 dollar floor.</strong> In Rafanello (2020), a dump truck's insurer argued a step-down capped its exposure at 35,000 because the driver was not listed. Local steps for <a href="/new-jersey/essex-county-truck-accident-help">truck crash claims in Essex County</a> are separate.</p>
<p>The court held that commercial vehicles in interstate or intrastate commerce must carry 750,000 dollars, listed driver or not. That covers a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,001 pounds or more, more than 10 passengers, or hazardous materials.</p>
<p>A light business van below that weight is outside the holding. With a truck, bus or hazmat carrier in that class, your own UIM may never be reached. Truck-specific steps are in our <a href="/new-jersey/new-jersey-truck-accident-help">New Jersey truck accident guide</a>.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-2">2</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section id="phantom">
<h2>What happens when a phantom vehicle shares the blame?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">Your UM carrier pays up to its limit for the missing driver's share.</strong> In Carbajal (2021), that was 15,000 of a 200,000 verdict, and the identified driver paid the other 185,000.</p>
<p>In Koukounias (2025), a merging phantom car forced a crash into a pole, but the jury found no permanent injury. How fault percentages are split is in our <a href="/new-jersey/partly-at-fault-nj-car-accident-real-fault-splits">NJ fault splits from real cases</a>; reporting steps are in our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-hit-and-run-accident-claim-help">New Jersey hit and run claim guide</a>.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-3">3</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section id="uninsured-owner">
<h2>I own an uninsured car. Am I always barred from suing?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">Only for injuries while operating it.</strong> In Memudu (2023), an uninsured owner killed in a second crash while retrieving his phone was not barred. The full rule for a hurt uninsured driver is in <a href="/new-jersey/uninsured-driver-hurt-in-nj-crash-can-you-sue">can you sue after driving uninsured</a>.</p>
<p>He was rear-ended on the Turnpike in Edison. About half an hour later, a second, separate crash killed him beside his disabled car.</p>
<p>Because he was not operating it then, the wrongful death and survivor claims went ahead.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-4">4</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section class="quiz-cta" id="quiz-mid">
<p>Did a step-down, a phantom car or a low limit leave you short after a New Jersey crash? A 30-second questionnaire checks whether a lawyer's office may review your claim for free.</p>
<p><a class="button" data-quiz-link="mid-article" href="https://quiz.injuriescases.autos/s/accident-newjersey?utm_source=injuriescases.autos&amp;utm_medium=referral&amp;utm_campaign=nj_mva_seo&amp;utm_content=nj-uninsured-underinsured-motorist-appeals-decisions">Start the New Jersey accident quiz</a></p>
<p class="cta-note">Advertisement. Opens the New Jersey questionnaire. Review its policies and contact consent before submitting your details. No legal advice or guarantee of acceptance or compensation.</p>
</section>
<section id="bad-faith">
<h2>Can I sue my UIM carrier for bad faith while the UIM claim is still open?</h2>
<p><strong class="df-k">You can file, but the court may sever it and stay discovery until the UIM claim is decided.</strong> That is what Tenenbaum (2026) required.</p>
<p>Two claimants pleaded common-law bad faith and the Insurance Fair Conduct Act alongside disputed UIM claims. The trial courts let bad-faith discovery run.</p>
<p>The appeals court reversed in the live case and dismissed the other as no longer live.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-5">5</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section id="release">
<h2>Can signing a release or filing late end a UIM claim?</h2>
<p>Yes. In Nesby (2019), an unconditional release of the at-fault driver ended the later claims, and in Chenel (2025) a late complaint failed. Other ways to fight an insurer's no are in <a href="/new-jersey/nj-car-insurance-claim-denied">how to challenge an insurance denial</a>.</p>
<p>In Nesby, the at-fault driver had no policy of her own. He took the 25,000 limit on the car she drove and released her.</p>
<p>He then sued her sister's and mother's insurers. He was not insured under those policies, so the claims failed.</p>
<p>In Chenel, the injured driver settled with the at-fault driver for 99,000 on a 100,000 policy, then pursued UIM. He offered no proof that Allstate's conduct kept him from filing on time.</p>
<p>Before you accept any payment, these cases point to four checks:</p>
<ol class="df-steps">
<li>The declared UM and UIM limit, which Motil held controls over a step-down.</li>
<li>The other vehicle: a commercial truck in the 750,000 class changes the math.</li>
<li>Written notice to your UIM carrier before you accept, a step Nesby traced to the Longworth cases.</li>
<li>The release wording: a reservation covering UIM and other insurers.</li>
</ol>
<p>What these settlements came to is in our <a href="/new-jersey/is-50k-good-car-accident-settlement-nj-appeals-figures">dollar figures from NJ appeals</a>. Broader questions are in <a href="/new-jersey/nj-8-questions-to-ask-before-accepting-a-settlement-offer">8 questions before accepting a settlement offer</a>.<sup class="df-fn"><a href="#src-6">6</a></sup></p>

</section>
<section id="threshold">
<h2>Does a UM or UIM claim still need a permanent injury?</h2>
<p>Often, yes. Three of the 13 UM and UIM appeals, all from 2025, were lost because the injury was not shown to be permanent.</p>
<p>Koukounias went to a jury, while Zavis and Joo ended on summary judgment. Joo had no medical proof that a prior condition was aggravated. The rulings are collected in <a href="/new-jersey/nj-verbal-threshold-appeals-rulings">13 NJ verbal threshold rulings</a>.</p>
</section>
<section id="faq" class="df-faqs">
<h2>Questions people also ask</h2>
<details class="df-faq" open><summary><h3>Is UIM coverage mandatory in NJ?</h3></summary>
<p>On a standard New Jersey policy, UM and UIM come with liability and PIP. The 2026 minimum limits are on our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-car-insurance-minimum-limits-2026">NJ minimum car insurance limits page</a>.</p>
</details><details class="df-faq"><summary><h3>How much uninsured underinsured motorist coverage should I have?</h3></summary>
<p>Carbajal shows what a low limit leaves: a 15,000 UM limit against a 200,000 verdict. How limits work, with DOBI's options, is in our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-uninsured-motorist-claim-help">NJ uninsured motorist claim guide</a>.</p>
</details><details class="df-faq"><summary><h3>What does uninsured motorist insurance not cover?</h3></summary>
<p>In these appeals, claims failed three ways: rights given up in a release (Nesby), a complaint filed too late (Chenel), and an injury not shown to be permanent (Koukounias, Zavis, Joo).</p>
</details><details class="df-faq"><summary><h3>What is the statute of limitations for uninsured motorist claims in New Jersey?</h3></summary>
<p>Chenel shows the cost of waiting: the UIM complaint came late and failed without proof the insurer caused the delay. The deadlines are in our <a href="/new-jersey/nj-car-accident-statute-of-limitations">New Jersey car accident deadline guide</a>.</p>
</details><details class="df-faq"><summary><h3>How do you sue an underinsured driver?</h3></summary>
<p>In these cases the order was: settle or tender with the at-fault driver's carrier, give your UIM carrier written notice before accepting (the Longworth step in Nesby), and reserve UIM rights in the release. Nesby lost by releasing without that reservation.</p>
</details></section>
